title: Operadic colimit cocones exhibit relative free algebras
statement:
Use the universe and presentably monoidal conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads and their algebra functor categories of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], and the monoidal cocartesian fibration of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Coherent transformations, mapping spaces and cocones have the meanings of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, an equivalence on the zero-fibers, both of which are spaces. Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and let $X:\mathcal C\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ be an algebra. An arrow in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is active when its opposite preserves both endpoints. For a color $d\in\mathcal D_{[1]}$ put $K_d=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d}$, where the active subcategory has all objects and just the arrows over active base maps. Write $T_d:K_d\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ for $X$ after source projection.

Here is the meaning of an operadically colimiting active cocone $T:K\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ with apex $v\in\mathcal V$. A finite tuple is an object in a fiber $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[r]}\simeq\mathcal V^r$, including the empty tuple. Concatenation $\oplus$ means concatenation of these tuples, with coherent structure induced by the Segal equivalences. For finite fixed tuples $L,R$ and $w\in\mathcal V$, restriction along the cocone must induce an equivalence from the space of active arrows $L\oplus v\oplus R\to w$ to the space of coherent active cocones $L\oplus T\oplus R\to w$. An active arrow from a tuple over $[r]$ to $w$ lies over the unique active map $[r]\to[1]$; a coherent active cocone is a coherent transformation with all components of this form. Empty $L$ and $R$ are allowed.

There exist a $\mathcal D$-algebra $F$ and a transformation of $\mathcal C$-algebras $\eta:X\to u^*F$ for which, at every color $d$, the cocone $T_d\to F(d)$ induced by $\eta$ and the action of $F$ is operadically colimiting in this sense. Moreover, for any $\mathcal D$-algebra $F$ and $\eta$ with this cocone property, composition with $\eta$ induces natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal V)}(F,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal V)}(X,u^*B)$ for every $\mathcal D$-algebra $B$.

source.place: Definitions A.2.1 and A.4.1; Propositions A.2.10, A.4.3 and A.4.4; Theorem A.4.6 (Gepner–Haugseng, printed pp. 88–92). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic theorem.

proof.text: Fix a color $d$. The active slice $K_d$ is small: it is a pullback of the small operads and an arrow slice of the small operad $\mathcal D$. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. The base diagram $pT_d$ has a coherent transformation to the constant $[1]$, whose components are the active arrows underlying the operations into $d$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to obtain $\lambda:T_d\to Q_d$ with cocartesian components and $Q_d:K_d\to\mathcal V$. At an input tuple $(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$, $Q_d$ is $X(x_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes X(x_r)$ by [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], with value $\mathbf1$ for $r=0$. The mapping-fiber assertion of the transport node identifies active coherent cocones on $T_d$ with ordinary coherent cocones on $Q_d$, naturally in their apex. This uses transport in a functor category, so it includes the higher simplices of $K_d$, rather than only its objects.

source.place: Proposition A.2.10, cocartesian transport to the fiber [1].

proof.text:
By presentability, $Q_d$ has a colimit $v_d$ since $K_d$ is small. Compose its colimit cocone with $\lambda$ to obtain an active cocone $T_d\to v_d$. For fixed tuples $L,R$, put $l=\bigotimes L$ and $r=\bigotimes R$, taking $\mathbf1$ for an empty tuple. The functor $z\mapsto l\otimes z\otimes r$ preserves small colimits: it is a composite of tensoring with fixed objects, each colimit preserving by the definition of presentably monoidal. Here is the fixed-context transport check. If $L,T_d(k),R$ have lengths $a,s,b$, concatenate the component of $\lambda$ with the fixed identity arrows to get an arrow $e$ over the block contraction $[a+s+b]\to[a+1+b]$. Choose a cocartesian lift $e_0$ of this contraction with the same source. The cocartesian mapping formula factors $e$ through $e_0$ by a vertical arrow from the target of $e_0$ to the target of $e$. Under each inert projection, composition of transports identifies this vertical arrow with the comparison of two lifts of the same selected identity or of the active map $[s]\to[1]$; those comparisons are equivalences. The Segal equivalence makes the vertical arrow an equivalence, so $e$ is cocartesian. Functor-category transport gives these comparisons coherently for all $k$. The cocartesian mapping formula, followed by composition of transports, therefore identifies restriction for the context $L\oplus T_d\oplus R$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(l\otimes v_d\otimes r,w)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_d,\mathcal V)}(l\otimes Q_d\otimes r,\Delta w).$$
This is an equivalence by the dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus the constructed active cocone satisfies the required two-sided context condition. In particular it satisfies the one-sided conditions of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. This works even for an empty slice, since tensoring preserves the initial object, and for nullary inputs, which transport to $\mathbf1$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.10 and the tensor-colimit argument of Corollary A.2.7; the two-sided version follows by applying both tensor factors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] to $u$ and write $\mathcal M_u$ for its correspondence. It is constant over $[0]$ precisely under the assumed equivalence on the space zero-fibers; both smallness and those hypotheses are retained. Its source active slice at $d$ is $K_d$ with the same diagram $T_d$. Therefore step 2 supplies the local cocones required by the existence assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling]. Obtain an operadic left Kan extension $H:\mathcal M_u\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ of $X$. Under the collage comparison its data are a $\mathcal D$-algebra $F$ and a coherent algebra transformation $\eta:X\to u^*F$; its local cocones are exactly the ones induced by $\eta$ and the action of $F$. This constructs the algebra and the unit together; independent choices of operations are not being asserted to be coherent.

source.place: Remark A.4.2, Theorem A.3.4(1), and the construction in the proof of Proposition A.4.4.

proof.text:
The left Kan extension from step 3 gives the one-sided operadic condition of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Empty context and [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identify its restriction map with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(F(d),w)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_d,\mathcal V)}(Q_d,\Delta w).$$
It is an equivalence for every $w$, so $Q_d\to F(d)$ is a colimit cocone by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For fixed tuples $L,R$, set $l=\bigotimes L$ and $r=\bigotimes R$, with value $\mathbf1$ for an empty tuple. Tensoring with fixed objects preserves small colimits by [def-coef-complete-algebroid], so $l\otimes Q_d\otimes r\to l\otimes F(d)\otimes r$ is colimiting. For lengths $a,s,b$ of $L,T_d(k),R$, concatenate the component of $\lambda$ with the fixed identities, over $[a+s+b]\to[a+1+b]$. Factor it through a chosen cocartesian lift of this block contraction, using the cocartesian mapping formula. Each inert projection of the intervening vertical arrow compares two cocartesian lifts of an identity-selected factor or of $[s]\to[1]$, hence is an equivalence. By the Segal equivalence of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the vertical arrow is an equivalence; thus the concatenated arrow is cocartesian. Functor-category transport supplies the coherent comparisons over $K_d$. Composing this transport with the active tensor transport identifies restriction in the simultaneous context $L\oplus T_d\oplus R$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(l\otimes F(d)\otimes r,w)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_d,\mathcal V)}(l\otimes Q_d\otimes r,\Delta w).$$
The dual cone criterion makes this an equivalence. Consequently the specific $\eta$ from step 3 satisfies the stated two-sided condition for every $L,R$, including the empty cases.

source.place: Definitions A.2.1, A.4.1 and Proposition A.2.10: recover the ordinary colimit and then tensor on both sides.

proof.text:
Now let $(F,\eta)$ be any pair with the stated two-sided property, and let $H=(X,F,\eta)$ in $\mathcal E=\mathcal E_{\mathcal M_u}(\mathcal V)$. Taking $L$ or $R$ empty shows that $H$ is an operadic left Kan extension. For any $G\in\mathcal E$ with source restriction $Y$, restriction defines
$$\rho:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal V)}(X,Y).$$
We prove it lifts every boundary $\partial\Delta^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. By the right-pinched mapping-space definition, the specified boundary on the left is a diagram on the proper faces of $\Delta^{n+1}$ that contain its final vertex. Keep the fixed final vertex $G$ and adjoin its entire initial face $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$ as the constant simplex at $H$; together these are $\partial\Delta^{n+1}$. The proposed $n$-simplex on the right gives a compatible diagram on $\mathcal C\times\Delta^{n+1}$ with that initial face constant at $X$. These data have exactly the domain in the relative boundary assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling], with $m=n+1>0$ and initial vertex $H$. Its filler is the required pinched $n$-simplex: it preserves the specified initial face and final vertex. For $n=0$ this same argument prescribes the two vertices and produces the missing edge. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a map lifting all such boundaries is a trivial Kan fibration and hence a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus $\rho$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces, with no passage to homotopy classes.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.4.3; Theorem A.3.4(2) and the relative prism argument of Higher Algebra, Lemma 3.1.3.16.

proof.text:
For a $\mathcal D$-algebra $B$, take $G_B=(u^*B,B,\operatorname{id})$ in the coherent comma description. The mapping formula of [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G_B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal V)}(X,u^*B)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal V)}(X,u^*B)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal V)}(F,B).$$
The first map to the common base is the identity, so projection to the last factor is an equivalence: the space of a point together with a path from it to a specified point is contractible, with inverse given by the constant path. Under this equivalence, $\rho$ of step 5 is $b\mapsto u^*b\circ\eta$. Step 5 says this map is an equivalence, which is the asserted adjunction formula. The comma comparison and its mapping formula are natural in $B$; restriction and composition are coherent functors. Therefore this identification is natural on the whole algebra infinity category, including its higher simplices. No separate choices of inverse maps are used to assert naturality.

source.place: Proposition A.4.3, comma mapping-space calculation in the proof of Higher Algebra Proposition 3.1.3.2.
